agree.reason: A skeptical HR manager sees a clear, honest teacher but also reads 'I have not kept GMP training records' with no counter-evidence, which confirms her assumption, and no start date or availability is given to make a phone screen easy.

honest.reason: The letter rightly drops the unsupported 'cut training in half' claim, and its figures (12 hours, 140 students, 41% to 58%, seven injury-free years since 2019) match the facts, though comparing a teacher onboarding to a production floor is a little loose.

works_the_facts.reason: It works out the 17-point gain but leaves out the strongest available figure, cutting new-teacher training from 20 to 12 hours (a 40% reduction), and never puts the training load in its best form.

right_comparison.reason: The only before-and-after is the AP pass rate, and the 20-hour to 12-hour training redesign, which is the comparison most relevant to this role, is missing entirely.

qualification.reason: The hedge 'I would spend my first weeks learning' has no date and nothing the reader can check, and it skips the real conditions: the GMP course that finishes May 2 and the June 14 earliest start.

objections.reason: It raises the no-GMP-records objection and simply concedes it, even though the facts answer it: signed training records for every trainee, two state audits with no findings, and GMP coursework already under way.

fit.reason: It is a one-page cover letter in the right form, but it uses 'Dear Hiring Manager' when Karen Doyle is named in the posting, leaves out the plant name and the applicant's name, and has no signature.
